correctness.rationale: For each N the boundary shift E_N obeys E_N^k(X)=(I_2/2)^tensor k tensor Tr_last-k(X) through k=N, then E_N^k=D_N thereafter. The uniform one-qubit rotation commutes with E_N, so t-fold channel powers are exactly a binomial mixture of the shift powers up to final unitary conjugation. This yields an upper half-diamond-norm bound P(Bin(t,g)<N) by the elementary maximal distance 2 between quantum channels, uniformly over arbitrary reference ancillas. The all-zero product input and the rightmost-L-zero projector yield a lower bound P(Bin(t,g)<=N-L)-2^{-L}; this is a legitimate trace-distance witness and therefore a diamond witness. Choosing L=floor(N^{1/4}) provides a vanishing measurement baseline with L=o(sqrt N). The binomial CLT at t=floor((N+s sqrt(N(1-g)))/g) makes both bounds converge to the same Gaussian tail G(-s). Monotonicity follows by CPTP postcomposition and invariance of D_N; inversion gives the stated expansion for every fixed tolerance in (0,1). Endpoints g=1 and g=0 follow from exact powers. Numerical checks reproduced 2732 assertions using the bundled standalone program, but these finite tests are not the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The model is Xie et al. arxiv:2609.37523 Eq. (10). Its main-text Section III and supplemental Section S2 analyze Floquet residual/pseudospectral disks and local-operator binomial propagation Eq. (S43). Neither part establishes the full-channel diamond-distance cutoff or matching Gaussian profile against all ancillas. Kastoryano--Reeb--Wolf arxiv:1111.2123 establishes quantum cutoff frameworks and tensor-power/commuting-generator estimates but no such assertion for this nonnormal non-tensor-power shift. Levin--Tankala arxiv:2109.05387 concerns different classical XOR-feedback shift-register processes; its Section 5 is exact finite-time classical mixing under another update. Published mathematical-finding searches found similar quantum erasure, timing-jitter and mixing-norm work, none with the same shift channel and time-profile implication. The claim is restricted to the sharp global operational profile, not to the source channel formula or binomial local propagation. The proof is short and an unlocated general quantum mixing/coupling theorem could subsume it; originality is best-knowledge, not independently certified.

value.rationale: The source model explicitly studies system-size dependent nonnormal Floquet response and spectrum, but its spectral atlas does not answer when the entire quantum memory loses distinguishability from complete depolarization. The half-diamond norm is the operational distinguishability of channels with entangled reference inputs. The theorem gives all fixed switch probabilities, a genuine mixing cutoff, a sharp order sqrt N window, a universal Gaussian profile, and the tolerance-dependent leading correction to mixing time. This is a complete naturally motivated observable for the full many-spin chain, and it highlights a linear storage-time scale despite all nonstationary eigenvalue moduli remaining size independent. The finite-N sandwich is reproducible and quantitatively useful. It is not an arbitrary finite slice or mere reproduction of the source spectrum; it does not claim a general theorem beyond the exactly solvable model.
